Section 24.6 text is written. Body: handbook/parts/p03/structures-definability-and-elementary-maps-w03-p03-006.tex, lines 1-389. Its heading is \chapter, as the packet specifies. It contains: conventions on reducts and named tuples; the elementary amalgam definition; a five-step diagram procedure; Amalgamation into an expansion (thm:p03-w03-p03-006-expansion-amalgamation); the Elementary amalgamation corollary (two clauses); Disjoint amalgamation over an elementary substructure; Amalgamating a family; Existential amalgamation, stated as an equivalence; Models of the universal part; Models of the restricted theory T^L, with a moreover clause; a worked DLO example with non-disjoint and disjoint amalgams over Q; a failure warning, where disjointness fails over a non-elementary common set (one-element predicate); the N/Z example of an embedding that cannot be made elementary; a relationships paragraph; and sources.

assessment_dispute: N-a-004-C01 (partial): the Section 6 presentation of Vaught 1961 is incomplete. (1) The handbook never says that the never-two theorem answers Raphael Robinson's question of whether some complete theory has exactly two denumerable models (p. 304; p. 318; footnote 23 dates the question to a 1957 conversation). n-a-004-01.tex:122-123 only calls the equivalence example 'Robinson's motivating contrast'. (2) The source's own justifications in the proof of Theorem 6.1 are missing: T_1 has one denumerable model by Cantor's theorem (p. 318), and models of T_n agree up to isomorphism by Skolem's theorem [14] (p. 319). Unattributed back-and-forth proofs replace them (annex n-a-004-01.tex:138-147). The source's sketch of T_3' completeness (pp. 319-320) is replaced by a different game proof (annex 186-207). (3) The categoricity conjecture loses the source's standing: 'unresolved', apparently made by a number of people (p. 320). (4) Vaught's Theorem 6.1 ranges over n in omega (fn. 5). thm:p03-vaught-finite-counts (99-105) states only positive n, and lines 124-126 call positivity essential, so the n = 0 instance is excluded. (5) MAP-02 and MAP-04 are partial.

assessment_dispute: N-a-004-MAP-02 (partial): the categoricity conjecture is not given in Vaught's exact formulation. Vaught (p. 320) covers theories categorical in some power aleph_{1+alpha} but not aleph_0-categorical, and counts non-isomorphic denumerable models. n-a-004-01.tex:133-136 says 'exactly aleph_0 countable models'. Under the presentation's own convention (line 7: countable includes finite unless 'denumerable' is specified), that wording also counts finite models. The source's qualifiers 'unresolved' and 'apparently made by a number of people' are dropped. The aleph_1-without-CH problem (131-133) and the separation from never-two are present.

assessment_dispute: N-a-004-MAP-04 (partial): the omega-Vaught formulation is not tied to the conjecture. n-a-004-01.tex:197-205 defines vo(sigma) and calls omega-Vaught a stronger bound than 'merely a countable Vaught ordinal'. Nowhere on the route does the handbook say that a countable Vaught ordinal is equivalent to sigma satisfying the (infinitary) Vaught conjecture, or that omega-Vaught strengthens that conjecture. The selected primary version says both (GRT arXiv:2606.15205v2, p. 2 and p. 4). So omega-Vaught is not related to, or distinguished from, the cardinal, perfect-set and infinitary formulations. Those three, and what CH does to the bare cardinal formulation, are present (lines 141-179; annex 230-272).

author.continuation: Block 1 wrote section 28.9. It covers effective quantifier elimination and the decision theorem, the elimination procedures for DLO, T_S (successor with 0), atomless Boolean algebras and Th(Z)/Th(N) with congruence predicates, and transfer of decidability between structures through interpretations. All proofs are in the annex. tools/check.py --tree handbook shows no findings in these files, and find_fused_spaces.py reports no hits. Several labels the packet names, such as thm:p03-dlo-qe and def:p03-quantifier-elimination in qe-categoricity-games.tex, are not on the static route, so the text refers to the on-route labels sec:qe-categoricity-01, thm:dlo-qe and thm:theoremhood-undecidable instead. Next block: (1) write effective QE with complete proofs for ACF_p and RCF; (2) add an undecidability-transfer example with a full proof; (3) prove the algorithmic bounds quoted in tab:p03-qe-catalog, or report each one as open. C001-C003 can only proceed once a legitimate copy of the Project Euclid open-access chapter pl/1235417272 is held locally. The lead could fetch it through a normal browser session and add it to held-sources. The research note's Continuation section lists the sources tried and what remains.

assessment_dispute: N-a-011-C01 (Lyndon 1959 p. 143): two of the author's claims are missing. First, his judgment that the positive-to-preserved direction is not difficult, while the converse, though intuitively nearly as obvious, is a matter of considerable difficulty. Second, his statement that Los's announced proof used methods quite different from his own. Body n-a-011-02.tex 11-17 presents its shorter list as the source's historical attributions.

assessment_dispute: N-a-011-C01 (p. 144 and nn. 2-3): three things are missing. (a) The paper's placement within Tarski's theory of elementary classes [12, 13], using numerous concepts due to Tarski, with elementary extension due to Tarski and Vaught [15]. (b) The paper's statement that its main line of reasoning is self-contained, while the technical definitions needed for rigor and the interpolation theorem (which it calls its cornerstone) come from the earlier paper [7]; body 21-36 does not say its language convention follows [7]. (c) The acknowledgments of discussions with Henkin and Tarski at Berkeley, and of Robinson suggesting the relativization at the 1957 AMS Summer Institute, Ithaca; body 15 records only the suggestion.

assessment_dispute: N-a-011-C01 (p. 146 n. 4): three claims are missing: that Q-maps and elementary extension, with various results, are special cases of Keisler's more far-reaching ideas [4]; that the constants w_a derive from A. Robinson's diagrams [11]; and that Proposition 3 is contained in Th. 1.11 of Tarski-Vaught [15].

assessment_dispute: N-a-011-C01 (p. 148): the source defines an elementary class of relational systems as the set of all relational systems in an elementary class. This definition is not stated, although Theorem 5 and Corollaries 5.1-5.3 use the phrase (body 173-175, 194-199) and the annex relies on it (annex 183-193, 'Hence C-bar in K').

assessment_dispute: N-a-011-C01 (p. 153 nn. 5-7): three things are missing. (a) The attribution of the undecidability paragraph's concepts to Tarski-Mostowski-Robinson [14]. (b) The remark that undecidability matters chiefly for finitely or recursively axiomatized theories. (c) The sources of the two external undecidability premises: Church [1] for the pure-predicate example, and [14, p. 84] with Tarski's reference, plus Novikov [10], for group theory. Body 329-332 says only that the premises are external.

open_components.gap: assessment_dispute: N-a-006-C01 (partial; owned by w03-p03-033): Complete this source's actual named presentation, preserving its own proof scope: the complete Categoricity in Power article, pp. 514-538, is not reconstructed in full. The proof chain (Lemmas 1.1-1.2, 2.1-2.8, 3.1-3.9, 4.1-4.6, 5.1-5.7) and Examples I-III are present with written proofs in handbook/parts/p03/presentations/n-a-006-01.tex 1-468 and handbook/annex/p03/n-a-006-01.tex 1-1362. These items of the article are absent or narrowed on the route. (1) Introduction, p. 514: categoricity in power introduced by Łoś [9] and Vaught [16] in 1954; their observation that dense linear order is aleph_0-categorical and is not categorical in any higher power; Łoś's question, which the paper answers; 'saturated' glossed as universal-homogeneous; the stated dependence of the method on an analogue of derived-space/Cantor-Bendixson analysis; footnote 1 (identity with the 1962 Chicago dissertation); footnote 2 (uniqueness of saturated models shown in [10] to follow from Jónsson [5]). (2) Section 1, pp. 515-518: completeness of kappa-categorical theories without finite models credited to Vaught [16] and Łoś [9]; Lemma 1.2 credited to [10] and footnote 5 (1.2(b),(c),(d) are Jónsson's conditions V, III, IV); the definition of a category of maps (identity and composition clauses) with footnote 7. (3) Section 2, pp. 518-523: footnote 8 (syntactic alternative); footnote 10 (open formulas give the same algebra; satisfaction in A agrees with T(A) only for open formulas unless A is a model); footnote 11; 'S(A) has a basis of power kappa(A) modulo aleph_0' (only the upper bound is stated); the dual statements of 1.2(b),(c),(d) for restriction maps; the remark that Definition 2.2 and many results stay valid in other categories of continuous onto maps between compact spaces; footnote 12 (terminology suggested by Example I; Jónsson's generalized algebraic extensions [6]); footnote 13 (rank and degree combined into a single rank by replacing 'set of isolated points' with 'a single point' in 2.2(2)); Theorem 2.8 as an analogue of the Cantor-Bendixson theorem; the stated automorphism sufficient condition for a consistent Q in F(A) to lie in a unique point of S(A), with its proof from 2.1, and footnote 14 (the weakened condition is also necessary). (4) Section 3, pp. 525-529: relation to Ehrenfeucht-Mostowski [3] and Ehrenfeucht [1],[2] (3.2, 3.4, 3.5 slight variants of [3]); footnote 16 (Ehrenfeucht's case X empty and his stronger automorphism-class result); footnote 17 (Vaught [10] proved the crux of 3.8 for kappa = kappa^aleph_0); 3.9 as a generalization of the dense-order argument; connected/anti-symmetric credited to Ehrenfeucht [1]; footnote 18 (Ehrenfeucht for 2^kappa-categorical, Scott for kappa^aleph_0-categorical theories). (5) Section 4, pp. 529-534: footnote 20 (prime models over countable A under a weaker hypothesis [18]); footnote 21 (an example shows total transcendence is strictly stronger than density of isolated points; 4.5 not obtained under the weaker hypothesis). (6) Section 5, pp. 534-538: Theorem 5.1 credited to [10] and footnote 22 (Jónsson's universal-homogeneous systems; equivalence with saturation by Vaught [18] and Keisler [8]); footnote 23 (Vaught's approach through saturation and his GCH limit-power theorem); footnote 24 (5.2 proved in [10] without total transcendence when kappa = kappa^aleph_0; an example of a theory that is not totally transcendental with kappa^aleph_0 != kappa and no countably saturated model of power kappa); the derived claim from 4.3 and 4.6 (a model A and X with kappa(X) = kappa(A) = kappa whose one-one self-maps of X extend to endomorphisms); question (5) as stated (the handbook drops kappa(A) = kappa(X) = kappa for each kappa >= aleph_0 and substitutes 'generated'); the remark that (5) would follow from 3.5 and 3.9 given a totally transcendental T^#; Ehrenfeucht's Theorem 2 of [1] and Vaught's discovery of a fallacy in its proof; footnote 25 (problems (1)-(4) are not due to the author; the handbook presents them as Morley's questions).

Block 1 wrote body 34.1-34.4 and the annex. Unit-compile reports ok. The fused-space check is clean. check.py's only hard finding for these files is the bib-key for the intake key Simon2015GuideManuscript. Next block, in this order:
(1) Write the NIP non-o-minimal ordered example (Q,<,P) with P dense and codense: QE by back-and-forth, NIP by Boolean combinations and the one-variable reduction. First read packet 036's file (34.5) to avoid writing the same treatment twice.

(3) Prove Shelah's Theorem 2.9, including the Erdos-Makkai lemma.
(4) Try to open a free copy of Shelah1971NonIsomorphicModels (Shelah archive), so it can be distinguished from its own text.
(5) Present the remaining Simon results: Proposition 2.55, Theorem 2.60, Proposition 2.69, Baldwin-Saxl, and the Example 2.12 and A.1 items.

author.continuation:
Section 34.9 written (new \chapter, label tag p03-w03-p03-037). It contains:
- RCF in {0,1,+,-,.,<}, axiomatized by the polynomial intermediate-value scheme (Coste 1999 p. 8).
- A full annex proof of quantifier elimination: polynomial lemmas (Rolle, mean value, monotonicity, Cauchy bound, square roots), sign tables, sublist maps, pseudo-division, a uniform sign-table theorem by lexicographic induction on (largest formal degree, count), then QE.
- Completeness, definable sets = semialgebraic sets, o-minimality of every model with a uniform D+1 convex-component bound, and RCF as an o-minimal theory.
- Worked monotonicity instances (x^3-3x and 1/x) and a 13-cell decomposition adapted to the circle and the disc.
- Instability via x<y, and one-variable NIP with an explicit 2D+3 bound.
- Failure of QE in the ring language, and the expansion of the real field by Z, which is neither o-minimal nor NIP. All of these are proved in the annex.

author.continuation: Section 35.9 was written from the held SRC-049 preview, which contains Barwise Ch. I and Ebbinghaus Ch. II; nothing was read online. It links to the existing compactness-failure and proof-boundary results rather than repeating them: bw-extended-ls, infinitary-rule, H-infinity completeness, hinf-soundness, hinf-uncountable and Karp. Four pieces are new: Ebbinghaus's well-ordering-number criterion (countable compactness iff no countable set of sentences pins down an infinite ordinal) with complete proofs, the formulas mu_beta and the result that sigma_alpha pins down every countable alpha >= 2, a worked example, and three other first-order transfers that fail (arbitrarily large finite models, Los, upward LS). Checks: unit-compile ok; find_fused_spaces reports no hits; check.py shows only the bib-key finding for this packet's own intake keys. Three referenced labels are off the static input route (thm:p02-fol-compactness, thm:p02-upward-ls, thm:p03-los), so the text cites thm:p03-compactness-ultraproduct and thm:p02-upward-ls-elementary-extension instead and proves the Los clause directly. Existing treatments not listed in the packet are recorded in the return file. Next block: when w03-p03-039/040 publish labels, replace the prose pointers with \\cref. The Ebbinghaus1985ExtendedLogics entry in this packet's bib intake is identical to the one in the w03-p03-044 intake; the merge should dedupe it.

author.continuation: No Baldwin ch. XII content was written: in this block all 13 components are blocked_source. Project Euclid served a bot-check page for every URL of the open-access 1985 chapter, and I did not attempt the check. No other legitimate copy was found. As general content for 36.8 MP-0 only, I wrote a partial presentation from Baldwin-Shelah 1985 (NDJFL 26, pp. 229-303). I read it from the published scan on Shelah's archive (https://shelah.logic.at/files/95815/156.pdf), pp. 229-244. The reader text says it follows that paper and not the chapter. author.continuation: Block 1 wrote the writable part of MP-0 for section 39.3 as a new \chapter and a matching annex. The chapter covers the L^k_{infty omega}/FO^k grammar with variable reuse, free labels, satisfaction, an infinitary quantifier rank and k-variable equivalence. It defines the k-pebble game with placement, reuse and removal, where the Duplicator wins only if every position is a partial isomorphism, and states the variants of the Technion slides and of Kolaitis. The finite-round theorem is proved: PG^n_k, its no-removal variant, L^{k,n} and FO^{k,n} are equivalent. The eternal theorem is proved for all three game variants against L^k-equivalence, plus the FO^k clause for finite structures. Worked examples (K_k vs K_{k+1}, even size, L_m vs L_n), the N vs N+Z limitation and the EF bridge are each proved in the annex. Sources read this session: the Kolaitis 2003 manuscript (TU Wien copy, pp. 3-4 and 52-61), Technion 236605 Lecture 4/5 slides, and Graedel's held ch. 3 (pp. 133 and 190). unit-compile is ok with 8 minor title overfulls. check.py --tree shows only bib-key findings, all for the four intake keys. The 35 SRC-050 components are readonly (owner w03-p03-054, A14). author.continuation:
MP-0 for 40.6 is written in the owned body and annex files. The source is Spencer's hosted version, fetched in this session from https://cs.nyu.edu/faculty/spencer/papers/ircsallsubm.pdf and read at pp. 1, 4-12 and 15-18 (sha256 b81de4d3...).

What the files contain:
- **Spectrum:** definitions of f_A and Sp(A).
- **Threshold:** the K_{3,k} threshold, proved by first and second moments, plus the sparse/safe equivalence.
- **Common neighbourhoods:** the maximum of |N(x1,x2,x3)| equals k on I_k.
- **Second-order side:** what EVEN and BIGGER say, the limit values of A*, and Sp(A*) on [1/3,1).
- **Not first-order:** A* is not first-order definable (EF game on complete bipartite graphs, using 038's game criterion).
- **Representation lemma:** proved almost surely under l(3α-1)<1 with 1/3<α<1/2, using conditioning on root edges and a binomial tail bound proved inline. Above 1/2: the l=0 case holds and the l=1 case fails, which corrects the source for k=4,5.
- **Encoding:** the first-to-second-order direction holds in every graph; the converse holds almost surely for k>=6.
- **Infinite spectrum:** Sp(A) on [1/3,1/2) is {1/3} together with 1/3+1/k for k>=7.
- **Also included:** a method entry, a worked example at α=π/7 (jump at 11/24), limitations, the Hella-Kolaitis-Luosto question reported as open, and relationships.
